title: Res and Sat are quasi-inverse: Coeff_G(B(Σ), Φ) ≃ Coeff_M⁰(B(M)) (Prop 8.2)
body_html:
$\Res$ and $\Sat$ are quasi-inverse

Proposition (Sheaf7 Prop 8.2). $\Res$ and $\Sat$ are quasi-inverse to each other; hence $$\Coeff_M^0(\mathcal{B}(M)) \;\xrightleftharpoons[\Res]{\Sat}\; \Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi).$$

This is the $\Phi$-isotypic incarnation of [[node:equivariant_sheaves.heisenberg_weil_equivalence|the §4 Heisenberg–Weil equivalence]] specialized to the data $(J, Q, \kappa)$ of this section.
proof_html:
Specialize [[node:equivariant_sheaves.heisenberg_weil_equivalence|§4 Heisenberg–Weil equivalence]] (Sheaf7 Prop 4.2) to:

  • $X = \BSigma$, $G$-action;
  • $J := \mathscr K_{\bullet,0+}$ (the cosheaf of $K_{\mathcal F, 0+}$);
  • $Q := \mathscr K_{\bullet,+}$ (the sheaf of $K_{\mathcal F, +}$);
  • $\phi := \phi$ (our character system);
  • $\check{\mathscr K} := \mathcal F \mapsto \kappa^*_\mathcal F$ (the dual $\kappa$-coefficient system from Dual coefficient system 𝒦*: F ↦ κ_F* (geometrization of (E3)));
  • $\mathscr K := \mathcal F \mapsto \kappa_\mathcal F$ (the $\kappa$ system itself).

Then the §4 abstract functors $\mathfrak R$ and $\mathfrak S$ specialize to our $\Res$ and $\Sat$ from Res and Sat functors between Coeff_G(B(Σ), Φ) and Coeff_M⁰(B(M)):

$$\Res(\mathscr V) = \mathbb{III}^*(\kappa^* \otimes \mathscr V)_J, \qquad \Sat(\mathscr W)_\mathcal F = \varinjlim_{(g, \mathcal F')} {}^g(\mathscr W_{\mathcal F'} \otimes \kappa_{\mathcal F'}).$$

Verification of hypotheses for §4. The abstract result applies once we check:

  1. $\kappa$ is a sheaf of $J$-Heisenberg–Weil types — this is axiom (E1)–(E2) of [[node:depth_zero_reduction.hypothesis_E]]: each $\kappa_\mathcal F$ extends the unique Heisenberg–Weil type $\eta_\mathcal F$ of $J_\mathcal F = K_{\mathcal F, 0+}$ with $\eta_\mathcal F|{K{\mathcal F, +} \cap K_{\mathcal F, 0+}} = \phi_\mathcal F$-isotypic.

  2. Compatibility along restrictions — (E3) gives the cInd intertwiner $\iota_{\mathcal F, \mathcal E}: \cInd_{\hat K_\mathcal F}^{\hat K_\mathcal F K_{\mathcal E, 0+}} \kappa_\mathcal F \xrightarrow{\sim} \kappa_\mathcal E|{\hat K\mathcal F K_{\mathcal E, 0+}}$ for $\mathcal E \preceq \mathcal F$. This is exactly the compatibility of §4 specialized to our $(\eta_\mathcal F, \phi_\mathcal F)$.

  3. The torsor is non-empty — (E4) plus the global $\beta$-extension existence from Global β-extension existence (compatible κ-family on B(G_β)) (= Skodlerack–Ye Thm 5.21 in the classical/quaternionic case, adapted to Yu/AFMO κ in the tame case via the same technique). This gives the object $\mathscr K = \kappa$ with $(\check{\mathscr K} \otimes \mathscr K)_J = (\kappa^* \otimes \kappa)_J = \mathbf 1$.

  4. (K4) — [[node:depth_zero_reduction.K4_hypothesis]] gives the reductive-quotient isomorphism $\hat M_\mathcal F / M_{\mathcal F, 0+} \cong \hat K_\mathcal F / K_{\mathcal F, 0+}$ needed to identify $\Coeff_M^0(\mathcal B(M))$ with $\Coeff_G(\BSigma, \mathbf 1_{QJ})$ after specialization.

All four hypotheses hold (the first three by construction of $\kappa$; the fourth as a standard structural fact of the K-cosheaf). Hence the §4 equivalence applies and $\Res, \Sat$ are quasi-inverse. $\square$

Where the proof matters

This is the middle arrow of the main reduction-to-depth-zero chain (Main Theorem 8.2.1: Rep_Φ(G) ≃ Rep_0(M)). The leftmost and rightmost arrows are localized equivalences (§7.4 + Schneider–Stuhler); this Prop 8.2 bridges $\Phi$-isotypic systems on $\BSigma$ to depth-zero systems on $\mathcal B(M)$.
